display.purpose: The Dashboard hero name only. Nothing else in the product reaches this size.

title.purpose: Card headings, project/company/tech names, social platform names.

body.purpose: About copy, card descriptions, chat message text. 14px / 1.65.

label.purpose: Tags, category pills, kbd hints, group labels, footer credits, timestamps. 10-13px, quiet.

label-sm.purpose: Category pills, group labels, compact meta. 11px / 600.

body-sm.purpose: Card sub-descriptions and chat message text. 13px / 1.5.

meta.purpose: Section subtitles, hints, secondary button labels. 12px.

shadows.name: panel-hairline-lift
shadows.purpose: The five page panels and three dashboard stat cards. The system's most-used shadow, deliberately quiet. Dark counterpart: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06), 0 16px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.50).

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Chat launcher, chat header controls, send button. Accent-tinted so it tracks the visitor's accent choice.

shadows.name: drawer-modal
shadows.purpose: Mobile sidebar drawer and award lightbox. The only genuinely dark shadow. Dark mode: 0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.7) plus a 1px white 4% ring.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Project, experience, and tech-stack cards on hover, paired with a 3-4px translateY and a border shift to --card-hover-border.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions - hover fills, border shifts, small lifts. ~0.28s.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: Entrance animations: page swap, stagger reveals. Slower, softer settle.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Overshoot easing. INCUMBENT, NOT RECOMMENDED FOR NEW WORK: the mechanical detector flags it as dated bounce/elastic easing, and it is correct that it overshoots. It is used in exactly two places - the sidebar nav icon hover tilt and the theme-toggle knob - and is documented here for fidelity rather than as a pattern to copy. Prefer ease-out for anything new.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric in-out, for rare cases that need equal accel and decel.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Small state flips - icon swaps, chip feedback, modal exit.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Rare; the slowest transitions in the system.

motion.name: modal-exit
motion.purpose: Modal and panel exit. Must stay in sync with MODAL_EXIT_MS in Dashboard.tsx and Awards.tsx.

narrative.overview:
An engine room is the part of a ship nobody photographs, and the part that decides whether the ship works. It is instrument-dense, hot-lit, and every panel is there because something depends on it. This system is built on that logic: no ornamental surface, no decorative gradient, no atmosphere for its own sake. What separates one surface from the next is a hairline and a tone step, the way a machine separates one plate from the next.

The default is monochrome and stays that way unless the visitor chooses otherwise. Ink black on white frost, one blue-grey hairline family, and a six-choice accent picker the reader controls. Colour is a dial, not a statement — a visitor who picks ocean blue gets a site that is still this site, only tuned. Density is the other load-bearing choice. Body copy sits at 14px, labels at 10px, card padding at 18px, and the base grid gap at 14px. This is a workbench that expects to be scanned, not a poster that expects to be admired.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome by default; the accent is a visitor-controlled dial, never a brand statement.
Depth comes from hairline borders and a single tone step, not from shadows. Shadows are reserved for genuinely floating things: the chat panel, the launcher button, the mobile drawer.
Small, tight type and small radii. Nothing is oversized for effect.
One font (Plus Jakarta Sans) at five weights; hierarchy is carried by size, weight, and letter-spacing, not by a second family.
Motion is short and eased-out; every animation has a prefers-reduced-motion off-switch.

rules.name: The Monochrome Default Rule
rules.body: No colour ships as the default state. Ink is the default accent; the five chromatic accents exist only as visitor choices, are applied identically in light and dark mode, and change nothing about layout, type, or density. Adding a sixth accent is a data edit plus a picker dot, not a redesign.

rules.name: The Accent Scarcity Rule
rules.body: The accent colour paints interactive and live elements only — active nav, focus outlines, the launcher, contribution level 4, the "available" dot. It is never a background for a large block of text.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: There is no second typeface, and there is no monospace face. Hierarchy is built from the five weights of Plus Jakarta Sans plus size and letter-spacing. Introducing a second family changes the product's character, not just its styling.

rules.name: The Small-Label Rule
rules.body: Metadata is set small and quiet (10-13px, Slate Soft or Slate Faint). A label never competes with a body paragraph; when in doubt, drop it a step rather than colouring it.

rules.name: The No-Display-Inside-Mid-Page Rule
rules.body: The 47px display treatment belongs to the Dashboard hero name alone. Section titles cap at 24px.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only as a response to state (hover, floating overlay, focus) or on the four genuinely floating surfaces named above. Never add a shadow to a static card to "make it pop" — that pass has been reverted here before.

rules.name: The Paired-Dark-Rule
rules.body: Every light-mode shadow or border rule is written together with its [data-theme='dark'] counterpart in the same change. An unpaired shadow reads as a smudge on black.

rules.name: The One Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every separable surface is separated by a 1px --border-color hairline and a tone step. Do not add a second separator to the same edge.

rules.name: The No-New-Spring Rule
rules.body: --ease-spring (cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)) overshoots and is documented in the sidecar for fidelity, not as a pattern. It is used in exactly two incumbent places - the sidebar nav icon tilt and the theme-toggle knob. Anything new uses --ease-out or --ease-out-soft.
